text: Meridian Polymers created a polymer formula for coating industrial parts. Sable Logistics relied on the restricted formulation to make its goods at its Ohio plant. The formula had been provided to Sable under written limits on external use. Production records show Sable's batches matched the restricted composition.

Plaintiff Meridian Polymers had developed a chemical mixing formula in 2011. Defendant Sable Logistics incorporated the confidential drawings into its own product lines for warehouse containers. The drawings were marked with plaintiff's internal circulation limits. Sable's engineers referenced them throughout the design phase without outside release.

In the mid-2000s, Sable Logistics ran production using plaintiff's restricted process sheets for a resin compound. Meridian Polymers had supplied the sheets with stamped internal-use-only notices. The defendant's plant in Texas followed the steps exactly. Output volumes rose once the bounded documents were put on the floor.

Meridian Polymers devised a curing formula for flexible circuits. Sable Logistics applied the confidential test data in its development of shipping labels in 2019. The data bore the originator's restricted-access legend. Internal memos show defendant's lab repeated Meridian's ratios in trial runs.

Sable Logistics used the marked-confidential schematics on its assembly line for servo brackets. Meridian Polymers had authored the formula-driven geometry in 2014. The schematics displayed the supplier's no-external-share marks. Defendant's supervisors distributed prints only within the assigned bay.

Plaintiff Meridian Polymers produced a bonding formula for sterile trays. At its plant, defendant Sable Logistics operated from the secrecy-bound engineering files to mix batches. The files stated they were not for outside circulation. Sable's operators followed the recorded weights through two production cycles.

Sable Logistics deployed the confidential customer data in its sales effort for polymer crates. Meridian Polymers compiled the linked formula preferences of buyers in 2017. The dataset carried the maker's limited-release tag. Defendant's reps quoted those mixture specs to four accounts.

Meridian Polymers held a viscosity formula for drill lubricants. Sable Logistics relied on the restricted formulation to make its goods sold to mining clients in 2020. The composition notes were stamped for internal review. Defendant's blend matched the capped ratios in audit samples.

In 2013, defendant Sable Logistics incorporated the confidential drawings into its own product for cooling fins. Plaintiff Meridian Polymers designed the formula-based profiles. The drawings showed the originator's do-not-distribute border. Sable's draft team copied the contour scores into CAD.

Sable Logistics ran production using plaintiff's restricted process sheets for adhesive film at a Nevada site. Meridian Polymers authored the formula steps in 2009. The sheets displayed internal-only handling. Defendant's line ran the timed cures as written for six weeks.

Plaintiff Meridian Polymers logged a reaction formula for packaging foam. Sable Logistics applied the confidential test data in its development of pallet wraps during 2016. The readings showed the owner's restricted circle note. Defendant's chemists adopted the catalysts from those pages.

Defendant Sable Logistics used the marked-confidential schematics on its assembly line for pump housings. Meridian Polymers set the formula layout in 2012. The prints bore the drafter's limited-use stamp. Sable's crew fabricated to the sealed callouts without external posting.

Meridian Polymers finalized a coating formula for sensor strips. At its Boston unit, Sable Logistics operated from the secrecy-bound engineering files to coat parts in 2015. The file header named the keeper's no-share rule. Defendant's process logs cite the locked mixture order.

Defendant Halcyon Motors applied the confidential test data in its development work derived from Solstice Aerodynamics' customer list materials. The data files displayed headers stating they were not for outside application. Internal memos confirm the files guided calibration choices. The relationship to the restricted set was documented by project engineers.

Solstice Aerodynamics, a biotech supplier, maintained a customer list. Halcyon Motors used the marked-confidential schematics on its assembly line; the schematics were tagged with clauses bounding their deployment to the original recipient. Line supervisors acknowledged the tags during testimony. The customer list rode with the schematic package as a reference appendix.

Halcyon Motors relied on the restricted formulation to make its goods in the cosmetics field, the formulation having travelled with Solstice Aerodynamics' customer list under cover labels forbidding transfer. Batch records show the formula measured into each mix. The label text was reproduced in the receiving department's intake scan.

Plaintiff Solstice Aerodynamics produced a customer list for drilling vendors. Defendant Halcyon Motors operated from the secrecy-bound engineering files that carried printed cautions against use by any party but the addressee. The files informed a subsea component design. Cross-references to the customer list sat in the file margins.

In a gaming hardware dispute, Halcyon Motors deployed the confidential customer data in its sales effort; the data set arrived with Solstice Aerodynamics' legend restricting exploitation to internal planning. Account managers queried the set weekly. The legend was visible on the export cover sheet received by the defendant.

Halcyon Motors worked from drawings bearing redistribution bars in its vehicle line; Solstice Aerodynamics had sent the customer list with the drawings under a footer limiting copying. The bars appeared on each released sheet. Production audits captured the sheets at three stations. The footer referenced the included list as attached.

Solstice Aerodynamics supplied a buyer roster to Halcyon Motors, which ran its plant off process sheets stamped 'do not use off-site.' The sheets rode with the roster as a controlled packet. Supervisors logged the sheets in daily. The stamp was initialed by the defendant's receiving clerk on arrival.

Halcyon Motors assembled test units from specs boxed 'limited circulation' that reached it with Solstice Aerodynamics' account directory. The specs set torque and fit values. The box label named the directory as enclosed. Build plans cited the specs as source for the unit shell.

Defendant Halcyon Motors fed trial results tagged 'internal only' into its design loop; those results came beside Solstice Aerodynamics' client index. The tag sat atop every page. Engineers noted the results shaped the cooling path. The index was bound behind the results as appendix B.

Solstice Aerodynamics' schematic set carried 'return if not assigned' notes; Halcyon Motors placed the set on its build floor with the customer list clipped to the front. The notes restricted shop use to the consigned party. Station leads signed for the set each shift. The clip held the list as a lookup aid.

Halcyon Motors measured batches using a formula wrapper marked 'consignee use,' received with Solstice Aerodynamics' contact file for the sector. The wrapper barred outside making. The file listed buyers by region. The formula dictated the base mix ratio on the line.

Plaintiff Solstice Aerodynamics forwarded engineering folders edged 'no external run' to Halcyon Motors, the folders holding the customer list as tab C. The defendant ran its shop from those folders. The edge text limited operation to the named site. Weekly logs show the folders open at the console.

Quillon Devices maintained a supplier network map covering regional bottlers. Sable Logistics operated from the secrecy-bound engineering files to route its own beverage deliveries. The files carried markings limiting their use to Quillon work. Sable's teams referenced the network layout while setting up distribution in 2019.

Plaintiff Quillon Devices compiled a restricted supplier directory for chip packaging. Defendant Sable Logistics applied the confidential test data in its development of freight models that mirrored Quillon's approved vendor list. The test data was provided under stated limits on external reuse. Sable used the material in 2021 planning cycles.

Sable Logistics relied on the restricted formulation to make its goods after obtaining Quillon Devices' supplier contact record. The record was marked for internal Quillon logistics only. In 2018 Sable printed the record and assigned its buyers to call the same plants. No claim is made here about how the list left Quillon.

Quillon Devices held a supplier network chart for clinical trial shipping. Defendant Sable Logistics deployed the confidential customer data in its sales effort targeting the same courier firms. The chart bore a stamp restricting circulation to Quillon staff. Sable's reps worked from the chart through late 2020.

Sable Logistics used the marked-confidential schematics on its assembly line for packaging routes that followed Quillon Devices' supplier map. The schematics stated they were not for outside production. In 2017 the defendant ran its warehouse off those drawings. The narrative notes only the use, not the source transfer.

Plaintiff Quillon Devices prepared a vendor routing book for beverage syrups. Sable Logistics ran production using plaintiff's restricted process sheets that listed approved suppliers and load steps. The sheets carried a footer limiting use to Quillon facilities. Sable's plant adopted the steps in 2016 without alteration.

Quillon Devices built a protected supplier index for drug logistics. Sable Logistics incorporated the confidential drawings into its own product by rendering the index in its tracking app. The drawings were tagged with a restriction notice. During 2022 the defendant shipped using routes from that index.

Sable Logistics printed Quillon Devices' capped supplier roll and sent trucks to those warehouses. The roll showed a stamped limit to Quillon dispatch use. In 2014 the defendant's coordinators followed the roll for winter routes. This account covers use on the ground, not any prior talks or pacts.

Plaintiff Quillon Devices issued a sealed vendor list for chip cold-chain. Defendant Sable Logistics applied the confidential test data in its development of a matching partner scorecard. The list displayed a clause restricting outside application. Sable's analysts referenced it across 2023 onboarding.

Quillon Devices kept a locked supplier ledger for trial supplies. Sable Logistics relied on the restricted formulation to make its goods by copying the ledger's lot assignments. The ledger noted it was Quillon-internal. In 2019 the defendant's sites fulfilled from those assignments only.

Sable Logistics deployed the confidential customer data in its sales effort by pitching Quillon Devices' bonded suppliers as its own. The data file showed a header limiting sharing. Throughout 2021 the defendant's pitches used the file's network. The text states use, not any employee exit or waiver.

Defendant Sable Logistics used the marked-confidential schematics on its assembly line mapping Quillon Devices' supplier bays. The schematics bore a use restriction for Quillon lines. In 2013 Sable laid out its yard per those bays. No note is taken of reverse engineering or public sources.

Quillon Devices circulated a capped supplier grid for component moves. Sable Logistics ran production using plaintiff's restricted process sheets to schedule pickups at the grid's nodes. The sheets carried a note barring external runs. The defendant's 2018 floor plan followed the sheets exactly.

Sable Logistics incorporated the confidential drawings into its own product showing Quillon Devices' supplier spine for medicine runs. The drawings held a restriction seal. In 2020 the defendant's platform traced shipments along that spine. The summary records incorporation, not any intrusion or license chat.

BlueFern Genetics engineered a closed seed-treatment line. Kestrel Dynamics operated from the secrecy-bound engineering files to run its own coating runs. The files carried internal circulation limits set by BlueFern. Kestrel's plant personnel followed those files during the 1998 season without external authorization.

Plaintiff BlueFern Genetics maintained a restricted steeping method for seed coat application. Defendant Kestrel Dynamics ran production using plaintiff's restricted process sheets at its Ohio facility in 2004. The process sheets were stamped with internal distribution controls. Kestrel's shift logs show the sheets governed two production campaigns.

Kestrel Dynamics, a toy maker, incorporated the confidential drawings into its own product line in 2011. The drawings derived from BlueFern Genetics' separate coating-equipment design group and bore internal access markings. Kestrel's engineers referenced them while building mold tools. The items were not released to the public.

BlueFern Genetics devised a temperature-controlled steep for treated seed. In 2019 Kestrel Dynamics used the marked-confidential schematics on its assembly line in Nebraska. The schematics specified valve timing and bath concentrations. Kestrel supervisors distributed the prints only to line leads under internal document rules.

Defendant Kestrel Dynamics relied on the restricted formulation to make its goods at a Michigan plant during 2007. The formulation had been issued by BlueFern Genetics under internal handling limits for coating mixes. Kestrel's batch records list the mixture identifiers. Production continued for eleven months under those records.

Kestrel Dynamics applied the confidential test data in its development of an automotive gasket line in 2016. The data originated from BlueFern Genetics' materials lab and was tagged for internal use only. Kestrel's project files show the values guided cure-cycle choices. The tests were not published outward.

In 2002 BlueFern Genetics circulated internal coat-weight tables to affiliated sites. Kestrel Dynamics, then a chemicals firm, operated from the secrecy-bound engineering files to set its reactor feeds. The files displayed internal routing codes. Kestrel's operators consulted them across a spring production cycle.

Plaintiff BlueFern Genetics designed a pelletizing die with access-limited prints. Defendant Kestrel Dynamics incorporated the confidential drawings into its own product for a toy launcher in 2020. The prints showed cooling-channel placement. Kestrel's tooling shop traced the geometry directly from the supplied sheets.

Kestrel Dynamics ran production using plaintiff's restricted process sheets for an automotive primer wash in 2010. BlueFern Genetics had assigned the sheets an internal read-only status. Kestrel's line managers scheduled tanks by those sheets. The campaign spanned two quarters at the Illinois site.

BlueFern Genetics issued bounded engineering files for a seed-soak centrifuge. In 2015 Kestrel Dynamics operated from the secrecy-bound engineering files to assemble its unit. The files noted internal loan status. Kestrel's build team copied settings from the bound volume during commissioning.

Defendant Kestrel Dynamics used the marked-confidential schematics on its assembly line for chemical dosing skids in 2009. BlueFern Genetics prepared the schematics with internal seal stamps. Kestrel's technicians mounted panels per the drawings. The line served a contained batch area for six months.

Kestrel Dynamics relied on the restricted formulation to make its goods for an automotive adhesive in 2014. BlueFern Genetics distributed the formulation with internal use flags. Kestrel's drum logs show the lot codes from those sheets. The mix ran on a dedicated weekend shift at the plant.

Plaintiff BlueFern Genetics generated confidential test data for a seed-enzyme bath. Defendant Kestrel Dynamics applied the confidential test data in its development of a chemical seed primer in 2021. The dataset carried internal reference bars. Kestrel's researchers entered the values into a lab notebook for trial batches.

Solstice Aerodynamics devised a pricing strategy for aerospace components. Marlowe Textiles incorporated the confidential drawings into its own product after receiving packets stamped with restricted-handling terms. The materials remained subject to Solstice's distribution limits throughout Marlowe's production run.

Plaintiff Solstice Aerodynamics had prepared restricted process sheets covering its aerospace pricing approach. Defendant Marlowe Textiles ran production using plaintiff's restricted process sheets at its weaving plant. The sheets carried Solstice's internal markings barring external reuse.

In the clean energy sector, Solstice Aerodynamics circulated test results on its pricing tactics with locked-header warnings. Marlowe Textiles applied the confidential test data in its development of inverter lines. The files were flagged as not for transfer beyond the named recipient.

Defendant Marlowe Textiles used the marked-confidential schematics on its assembly line that Solstice Aerodynamics had supplied for aerospace pricing layouts. The schematics bore Solstice's restricted-circulation seal. Marlowe's floor supervisors referenced them daily through the build season.

Solstice Aerodynamics, active in textile machinery pricing, sent formula cards to Marlowe Textiles with cover notes limiting use. Marlowe relied on the restricted formulation to make its goods under a tagged-batch system. The cards stayed inside Solstice's stated handling boundary.

Marlowe Textiles operated from the secrecy-bound engineering files that Solstice Aerodynamics had shared for clean-energy pricing plans. The files carried Solstice's do-not-distribute footer. Marlowe's team drafted bids using those files across two quarters.

Marlowe Textiles wave-loomed cloth following Solstice Aerodynamics' cost sheets, which arrived with a red perimeter marking the items as off-limits to others. The aerospace-origin pricing tables were sewn into Marlowe's planning. Solstice's courier slip noted return required.

Defendant Marlowe Textiles printed hang-tags using Solstice Aerodynamics' rate card, a document boxed with a stencil reading 'restricted circulation only' from the clean-energy pricing set. Marlowe's merch line quoted those numbers. The card never left Solstice's named-recipient list.

Solstice Aerodynamics forwarded sample panels with pinned-on slips stating the textile pricing grid was not to leave the room. Marlowe Textiles cut its own runs from those panels. The slips stayed attached through Marlowe's whole shift.

Marlowe Textiles fed its model with Solstice Aerodynamics' scenario tables, each page clipped with a band showing the trading-algorithm pricing was for named eyes. The firm's analysts referenced them in memos. Solstice's dispatch log flagged the band as binding.

Plaintiff Solstice Aerodynamics issued layout folios with a corner stamp limiting aerospace pricing reuse. Defendant Marlowe Textiles hung the folios at its line and used the marked-confidential schematics on its assembly line for fixture placement. The stamp stayed visible to staff.

Marlowe Textiles blended dyes following Solstice Aerodynamics' mix note, a page edged with a line stating the textile pricing mix was account-locked. The note rode inside Solstice's sealed envelope. Marlowe's mixer kept the edge intact through batches.

Solstice Aerodynamics shared drive folders with a header noting clean-energy pricing files were seat-assigned. Marlowe Textiles opened them and operated from the secrecy-bound engineering files to set its quote sheet. The header remained on every printout Marlowe made.

In 2020, Drayton Instruments within medical devices obtained a folio of Harrow Foods prescribers bounded by a use-by-recipient band. The firm posted the folio to its shared drive and cited it in sales calls. The band printed on the folio edge in Harrow's format.

NorthPeak Semiconductors says Drayton Instruments applied the confidential test data in its development of a sensor array back in 2017. The dataset bore a clear limitation notice from the original owner. Engineering memos reference the numbers throughout the build.

On the assembly floor, Drayton Instruments used the marked-confidential schematics on its assembly line through much of 2020. NorthPeak Semiconductors had issued the prints with internal handling rules. Supervisors acknowledged the source in shift reports.

Drayton Instruments relied on the restricted formulation to make its goods sold under a private label in 2016. NorthPeak Semiconductors had circulated the formula with a do-not-distribute footer. Batch receipts tie output to that exact mixture.

Drayton Instruments deployed the confidential customer data in its sales effort across the EU in late 2018. The records were tagged with NorthPeak Semiconductors' no-share clause. Account lists matched the protected set item by item.

The 2019 audit showed Drayton Instruments fed NorthPeak's limited-release measurement tables into its calibration rig. The tables were issued with a circulation cap. Technicians printed them on the controlled-access printer.

NorthPeak Semiconductors flagged that Drayton Instruments ran its fab using the capped process packet sent years earlier. The packet displayed a handling restriction from the semiconductor house. Yields tracked the enclosed recipe.

In a 2015 program, Drayton Instruments assembled test boards from the bounded spec pack it received under seal. The pack carried NorthPeak's external-transfer block. Reviewers noted the layout mirrored the protected pages.

Drayton Instruments put NorthPeak's closed-loop sample results into its own design tool in 2020. The results were marked for internal use only by the original firm. Code commits cite the figures as inputs.

NorthPeak Semiconductors noted Drayton Instruments placed the locked reference diagrams on its build station in 2018. The diagrams showed a withdraw-only footer from the chip company. Line scans reproduced them on finished parts.
Drayton Instruments cooked its lot using the sealed mixture note from NorthPeak's 2017 drop. The note bore a redistribute-prohibited stamp. Quality logs name the same blend proportion.

Cascade Biotech discovered that Redgate Software had incorporated the confidential drawings into its own product. The drawings carried Cascade's internal markings restricting external use. Redgate's engineering team referenced them while finalizing a related module last year.

Redgate Software ran production using plaintiff's restricted process sheets at its Austin facility in 2019. The sheets were stamped with limitations on transfer outside Cascade Biotech. Operators followed the steps verbatim during a three-month build cycle.

Cascade Biotech reported that Redgate used the marked-confidential schematics on its assembly line for a sensor line in 2018. The schematics bore Cascade's distribution limits. Production supervisors acknowledged following the layouts weekly.

Redgate relied on the restricted formulation to make its goods at a contract plant in 2022. Cascade Biotech had issued the formulation with bounded-access terms. The defendant's batch records show direct adoption of the mixture ratios.

Cascade Biotech's records show Redgate operated from the secrecy-bound engineering files to ship a firmware update in 2017. The files carried Cascade's internal circulation caps. Redgate's release matched the file contents closely.

Redgate deployed the confidential customer data in its sales effort across the Midwest in 2021. Cascade Biotech had tagged the data with no-external-sharing rules. Account teams imported the lists into their outreach platform.

Redgate took Cascade Biotech's bounded-access build scripts and ran them inside its own compiler toolchain through much of 2020. The scripts were issued with internal-only tags. Output binaries mirrored the original logic.

Cascade Biotech found that Redgate reused the limited-circulation module maps to configure its analytics service in 2019. The maps were handed over with stay-in-house conditions. The service's routing matched the maps precisely.

Redgate worked from Cascade Biotech's in-house-only calibration routines to tune its beverage filler controllers during 2022. The routines were marked for internal use. Technicians copied the timing values into their setup logs.
Cascade Biotech alleged Redgate adopted the locked-down assay code to power its screening app in 2018. The code carried non-export labels. The app's backend returned identical call patterns.

Redgate drew on Cascade Biotech's capped-access interface definitions to build its partner portal in 2021. The definitions were sent with do-not-share footers. The portal's endpoints reproduced the specified behavior.

Cascade Biotech said Redgate executed the restricted wafer-layout instructions on its fab line in 2017. The instructions bore internal-boundary stamps. Yield curves tracked the prescribed sequences exactly.

Redgate utilized Cascade Biotech's enclosed-distribution trial logic to drive its recruitment platform in 2020. The logic shipped with perimeter-use notes. The platform's scoring matched the original functions.

BlueFern Genetics developed a soy trait formula under internal locks. Orizon Energy incorporated the confidential drawings into its own product last year, using files that carried the plaintiff's restricted-marking protocol. The materials had not been released to outside parties.

Orizon Energy, a biofuels startup, ran production using plaintiff's restricted process sheets at its pilot plant in 2019. BlueFern Genetics had issued the sheets with stamp-based access limits. The batches were completed without any public disclosure of the underlying mixture.

In 2022, Orizon Energy deployed the confidential customer data in its sales effort for a fuel blend. BlueFern Genetics originated the contact list with access tiers. The defendant printed the records for its reps without a conference posting.

Orizon Energy incorporated the confidential drawings into its own product during a 2019 clean-energy turbine program. The drawings carried Almara Labs' internal restriction markings. Production records show the components were built to those drawings at Orizon's facility outside Barcelona.

Orizon Energy pulled its 2015 bracket cuts from Almara's closed-index file set in the aerospace shop. The set carried Almara's internal lend-only mark. Cut plans at Orizon named the same file codes from that marked set.
